issues.detail: The Greek 'ενενευον' (eneneuon) means 'to ask/inquire' (from enēxeō), not to 'make a sign' or 'signify' (ra dấu). The Vietnamese translation changes the action from an inquiry into a physical gesture.

The Greek phrase 'το τι αν θελοι καλεισθαι' means 'what he wants to be called', but the Vietnamese 'muốn gọi nó là gì' translates it as 'what [he] wants to call him/it'. This shifts the direction of the action: the Greek is about the name the subject *wants for himself*, whereas the Vietnamese suggests what the father *wants to call the subject*.
